mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.1% compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns as investors price in continued monetary accommodation.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.1% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 5.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns within 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 5.5%, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate a collapsing housing market that triggers broader economic slowdown expectations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in RSAFS and HOUST fails to generate negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction effect is statistically insignificant (p>0.05) in a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 during post-pandemic supply shocks indicates persistent production bottlenecks that increase inflation and reduce corporate margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: In periods of INDPRO below 100, S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) above 2% annualized signals robust economic expansion that boosts corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 growth exceeds 2% annualized, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) falling below 95 indicates severe supply disruption that increases inflation risks and recession probability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns within 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO is below 95, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 260) combined with ultra-low rates (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) creates a central bank dilemma where equity markets price in continued stimulus, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL > 260 and FEDFUNDS < 0.5, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained payroll growth (PAYEMS increasing for 3 consecutive months) during early economic expansion boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods of sustained payroll growth (PAYEMS increasing for 3 months), S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 40% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.
